primaryQuery: replace device in Home Assistant without rebuilding automations
readerQuestion: A bulb, sensor, plug, switch, lock, or other endpoint failed. How can I replace it without rebuilding its automations, scenes, dashboards, and history?
selectedBecause: The same replacement problem recurs from a long-running Home Assistant feature request through fresh 2026 Reddit and Home Assistant Community questions about same-model swaps, cross-brand replacements, history, and device IDs. Exact-query Google results remain dominated by partial forum workarounds and entity-renaming documentation rather than a current, homeowner-safe end-to-end workflow. Home Assistant 2026.7 and 2026.8 add durable area targets, better dependency discovery, and user-controlled entity IDs, but they do not add a universal physical-device replacement wizard. Search Console and the ownership maps were reviewed first: they contain no direct query or ownerPath for this intent, while their high-impression query families already belong to existing pages. The question is broad, recurring, durable, closely aligned with Tara's maintainable local-home approach, and distinct from Tara's coordinator, Thread border-router, host, and Matter-controller migration guides.

demandSignals.evidence: A May 2026 homeowner asks how to replace a failed device with the same model without rebuilding automations; replies immediately split the answer between stable entity IDs and direct device-ID references.
A March 2026 poster reports that removing a device left hundreds of device-ID references to repair and asks why Home Assistant cannot convert or replace those references automatically.

A May 2026 discussion asks for a replacement-safe abstraction that preserves dashboards, automations, and history when a physical device changes; the replies expose important history and identifier caveats.

The Home Assistant frontend issue documents how deleting a device can leave direct device actions empty and make the visual automation editor fail to save cleanly, corroborating the practical repair problem.

The exact-query review returned Home Assistant Community and Reddit workaround threads rather than a current standalone guide that separates entity, device, area, dashboard, scene, and history references.

searchReview.query: replace device in Home Assistant without rebuilding automations
searchReview.intent: Replace one failed or upgraded smart-home endpoint and keep its existing automations, scripts, scenes, dashboards, areas, voice exposure, and useful history working.
searchReview.resultGap: Current results give pieces of the answer: reuse an entity ID, avoid device IDs, or inspect a particular protocol. They do not provide one current workflow that starts with backup and dependency discovery, distinguishes entity references from direct device references and area intent, tests the new device before removal, handles scenes and dashboards, treats long-term statistics separately, and explains that Home Assistant 2026.8 still has no universal physical-device replacement wizard.

officialSources.name: Home Assistant 2026.8 release notes
officialSources.supports: Home Assistant 2026.8 improves entity-ID control and Search or Related discovery, warns that direct device-ID references may need attention, and describes its new device-registry work as groundwork rather than a finished physical-device replacement workflow.

officialSources.name: Home Assistant 2026.7 release notes
officialSources.supports: Purpose-specific automations can target an area so the intent can survive when a sensor is removed or swapped and the replacement is assigned to the same area.

officialSources.name: Home Assistant entity customization documentation
officialSources.supports: The UI allows an entity ID to be changed, while a friendly-name change alone does not affect references; existing automations and scripts must be checked when an entity ID changes.

officialSources.name: Home Assistant automation trigger documentation
officialSources.supports: Device triggers are tied to a device rather than necessarily to an entity, which is why reusing an entity ID cannot repair every automation reference.

officialSources.name: Home Assistant action target documentation
officialSources.supports: Actions can target entities, devices, areas, floors, and labels, and those target types have different replacement behavior.

officialSources.name: Home Assistant grouping documentation
officialSources.supports: Areas, floors, labels, and groups can organize or target devices and entities, providing more durable intent than one physical endpoint in appropriate automations.

officialSources.name: Home Assistant backup documentation
officialSources.supports: A manual backup provides a recovery point before a device replacement changes configuration, automations, scripts, or dashboards.

officialSources.name: Home Assistant device automation developer documentation
officialSources.supports: Home Assistant is exploring alternatives to legacy device automations; existing ones remain supported, but new device automations are no longer accepted from integrations.

officialSources.name: Home Assistant long-term statistics discussion
officialSources.supports: Reusing an old entity ID can preserve a statistics identity in some cases, but replacement history requires separate validation and should not be promised for incompatible units, classes, or overlapping entities.

existingCoverage.decision: Those pages replace a Zigbee coordinator, a Thread border router, the Home Assistant host, or a Matter controller, or troubleshoot missing trigger choices. None explains how to swap one bulb, sensor, plug, switch, lock, thermostat, or similar endpoint while preserving its consumers. The new page will own the single-endpoint replacement workflow and link to the infrastructure guides only when a reader is replacing one of those different layers.
